claim: The API returns workout data tracked with Suunto devices as FIT files.
quote: Application interface (API) provides you possibility to access the workout data tracked with Suunto devices. The API provides you the FIT files common in sports industry.

claim: FIT files contain GPS tracks and measured samples.
quote: These also have all the measured samples such as heart rate, r-r data, power data, altitude, temperature. These files also contain GPS tracks.

claim: Authorization is based on OAuth2.
quote: API authorization is based on OAuth2.

claim: Access is for companies and organizations building for a public audience.
quote: The API will be provided to companies, organizations who are providing tools / apps / services for public audience.

claim: Suunto does not offer access for personal use.
quote: We currently don't offer the API access for personal use.

claim: Applicants are reviewed on brand fit, customer interest and innovation mindset.
quote: We are reviewing the applicants based on for example the fit to our brand, interest from our customers and illustration of the innovation mindset

claim: Suunto does not charge for the API.
quote: We do not charge from the use of the API.

claim: Applying includes accepting the API agreement.
quote: When submitting your application you need to accept the API agreement.

claim: Applications are reviewed weekly with a maximum two-week wait.
quote: The applications are reviewed on weekly bases, so you have to wait few days prior getting the acceptance. There is maximum two week waiting period.

claim: Accepted partners hear back within two weeks.
quote: If you have been accepted to the Suunto partner program, you should get the response in within two weeks.

claim: The Development API has every endpoint but smaller request limits.
quote: The Development API includes all the endpoints but has smaller request limits.

claim: You submit your application information and subscribe to the production API.
quote: When you are ready you need to submit your application information in your profile page. Then subscribe to the production API.

claim: Suunto then grants production access and publishes the app on Suunto.com.
quote: After this we will grant you access to production API and publish your application to Suunto.com.

claim: One account can have only one app.
quote: One account can have only one app. One account is associated to one email address.

claim: An agency's client company applies and signs the API agreement.
quote: Please ask your client company to submit the partner program application, so that they can sign the API Agreement.

claim: Selecting the Suunto Cloud API on the application provides the API agreement.
quote: If you select Suunto Cloud API you will be provided the API agreement.

claim: Every data call needs the subscription key.
quote: To be able to use Integration API you have to subscribe to the API and add the subscription key to each request.

claim: Two keys allow regeneration without downtime.
quote: The purpose of having 2 keys it to allow key regeneration and redeployment without app downtime.

claim: OAuth requests do not need the subscription key.
quote: Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key parameter is required for Cloud API requests but not for OAuth related requests.

claim: Set app name, client secret and redirect URI; the client ID is generated.
quote: The Client Id is generating automatically.

claim: The authorization host is https://cloudapi-oauth.suunto.com.
quote: Authorization API has the address https://cloudapi-oauth.suunto.com.

claim: The authorization URL takes response_type=code, client_id and redirect_uri.
quote: https://cloudapi-oauth.suunto.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=<REDIRECT_URI>

claim: The token exchange uses HTTP Basic client credentials.
quote: The endpoint is protected using Basic authentication scheme in the following format:

claim: The token endpoint is https://cloudapi-oauth.suunto.com/oauth/token.
quote: curl -v https://cloudapi-oauth.suunto.com/oauth/token --user <CLIENT_ID>:<CLIENT_SECRET> -d grant_type=authorization_code

claim: The example response has expires_in 86400 and the workout scope.
quote: "expires_in": 86400, "scope": "workout"

claim: The JWT's user claim is the Suunto App username.
quote: You may parse it and extract a custom claim named ' user' which is the authorizing user's Suunto app account username.

claim: Users must use Suunto App credentials, not Movescount.
quote: Common issues are users using the Movescount credentials, these do not work. User needs to use the Suunto App credentials.

claim: There is no mobile SDK; authorization is optimized for mobile use.
quote: The authorisation process is optimized for mobile use. There is no mobile SDK at the moment.

claim: The integration API is at https://cloudapi.suunto.com.
quote: The integration API has the address https://cloudapi.suunto.com.

claim: Data calls need the Authorization and Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key headers.
quote: Making requests to the APIs requires using two HTTP headers:

claim: The workout list is at /v2/workouts.
quote: curl -v https://cloudapi.suunto.com/v2/workouts

claim: You can get workouts and daily activities.
quote: You can get workouts and daily activities.

claim: Daily activity contains steps and calories.
quote: This contains daily steps and calories.

claim: You can push routes and workouts.
quote: You can push routes and workouts.

claim: Routes are GPX files with waypoints that sync to watches for navigation.
quote: The routes are GPX files which have route location data enriched with waypoints. The routes are shown in Suunto App and can be then synched to Suunto watches for navigation.

claim: Workouts can be pushed as FIT files.
quote: You can push the workouts in FIT file format for the users account.

claim: Sleep data is not available yet.
quote: The Suunto Cloud API doesn’t yet support the sleep data fetch/push.

claim: Points of interest are not available yet.
quote: The Suunto Cloud API doesn’t yet support the point of interests.

claim: Personal data such as weight or heart rate zones is not available.
quote: Personal data such as weight data or heartrate zones are not available yet from Suunto Cloud API

claim: Use the workout list for history.
quote: To get list of the workouts from the past history.

claim: FIT files have the most comprehensive dataset.
quote: Fit files has most comprehensive dataset from each workout. Consisting all the sample data, laps and summary value from each exercise.

claim: Workout JSON has startTime and stopTime in epoch milliseconds.
quote: startTime is an integer in UNIX epoch milliseconds specifying when the workout was started.

claim: timeOffsetInMinutes is the UTC offset when the exercise stopped.
quote: timeOffsetInMinutes is an integer in minutes specifying the user's local time difference to UTC at the time when the exercise stopped.

claim: Workout contents depend on the watch model.
quote: The workouts are stored with Suunto watches and depend of the model.

claim: Sport modes can stop GPS or heart rate measurement.
quote: This makes it possible for example stop GPS tracking or heartrate measurements.

claim: Webhooks notify you about new workouts.
quote: Use the webhook method to get a notification about new workouts.

claim: The webhook is set in your app's OAuth settings and must be public.
quote: You can setup the webhook in your app oauth settings under your profile in Suunto Apizone

claim: The notification POST carries username and workoutid.
quote: Suunto partner notification has two parameters passed in the POST request username and workoutid.

claim: There is no webhook for daily activity.
quote: There is no webhook / notification model in place for activity data.

claim: Fetch daily activity with workouts, and about once a day otherwise.
quote: You can additionally fetch the daily activity for the user i.e. once a day, just in case user has synched their device with Suunto app wihout workouts.

claim: Suunto asks partners to avoid unnecessary polling.
quote: Avoid unnecessary polling of the API

claim: The developer API has the same capabilities but is rate-limited.
quote: There developer API has same capabilities as the production API. However, the number of calls you can do with developer API are rate-limited.

claim: Expect larger volumes at weekends and the start of the year.
quote: You can expect a larger data volume on weekends as people are more active and doing more workouts.

claim: Spikes at the start of the year.
quote: There is also spikes for example in start of the year

claim: Partners are added to a newsletter about new capabilities.
quote: Once you register to Suunto partner program, you will same time be included to newsletter which we are sending for participants when there are new capabilities available.

claim: Movescount is a completely separate system.
quote: There is nothing common with these. Movescount is completely separate system.

claim: Suunto encourages the Suunto App and Cloud API.
quote: we encourage people to change into Suunto App and therefore the Suunto Cloud API will be the way for Suunto Compatibility.

claim: China uses a separate API with different endpoints.
quote: We will then provide you the access to our Chinese API. This is technically the same, just with different address endpoints.

claim: A 500 usually means a bad workout key, a 12-byte hex string.
quote: Workout key format: hexadecimal string, key length - 12 bytes.

claim: Development runs against the production system with real tester data.
quote: The development with the API is done with the production system, so you can use the real data from your testers with your app/service.

claim: Suunto publishes example FIT files.
quote: There is also example FIT files available

claim: SuuntoPlus data sits in FIT developer fields.
quote: The Suuntoplus data is stored in FIT files as developer fields.

claim: API reference access requires partner acceptance.
quote: In order to get access to try the API you need to be accepted for Suunto partner program.
